agent.description: Who runs the conversation: nodespace, or a terminal harness (claude-code, codex, ...)
agent.name: agent

model.description: Model identifier used for this conversation, when known
model.name: model

options.description: The choices offered with a clarifying question; the question is the content
options.name: options

outcome.description: How the turn that produced an assistant message ended
outcome.name: outcome

reasoning.description: The model's chain-of-thought toward an assistant message
reasoning.name: reasoning

pending_delete->/out.description: Nodes the message asked to delete, held until the user answers

edgeFields.description: The node's version when the delete was proposed
edgeFields.name: version

edgeFields.description: How many nodes beneath it the delete was shown to remove
edgeFields.name: descendant_count

pending_delete->/out.name: pending_delete

resolved->/out.description: Nodes the message's turn looked up

edgeFields.description: The read tool that surfaced the node
edgeFields.name: tool

resolved->/out.name: resolved

edgeFields.description: Each write the message made to the node, in call order: its tool, summary, canonical_args and the edges it replaced
edgeFields.name: writes

context_tokens.description: Approximate token count of conversation context
context_tokens.name: context_tokens

pins->/out.description: Nodes this chat is bound to: a pinned skill is always offered, and any other pinned node is always in view
pins->/out.name: pins

exit_code.description: Exit code of the terminal session's process, once it has ended
exit_code.name: exit_code

session_id.description: The agent's own id for the conversation, which its resume flag takes: names state on this machine, so it stays here
session_id.name: session_id

session_status.description: Whether the terminal session is running
session_status.name: session_status

transcript.description: Raw terminal scrollback: may hold secrets, tokens and absolute paths, so it stays on this machine
transcript.name: transcript

capture_content.description: How much of a captured session is saved.
capture_content.name: capture_content

capture_enabled.description: Whether a finished terminal session is saved to its chat node.
capture_enabled.name: capture_enabled

providers.description: The OpenAI-compatible providers this database has configured.

itemFields.description: A UUID. Chats refer to the provider as `openai-compat:<id>`.
itemFields.name: id

itemFields.description: Display name in the model selector.
itemFields.name: name

itemFields.description: Sent as a bearer token. Empty when the endpoint needs none.
itemFields.name: api_key

itemFields.description: The `model` field sent to the endpoint.
itemFields.name: model

itemFields.description: The routing probe's verdict per served model. Dropped when the endpoint or model changes.
itemFields.name: routing_ok

providers.name: providers

required_extensions.description: Ids of the extensions a reader needs in order to read this database correctly. Empty by default. Core assigns no meaning to any entry; it refuses to open a database that lists an extension it does not support.
required_extensions.name: required_extensions

decision_status.description: proposed while under discussion; accepted once agreed; superseded once a newer decision replaces it, which locks it.
decision_status.name: decision_status

commits.description: The commits that deliver the issue, each a title and URL. Written as the whole list.
commits.name: commits

pull_request.description: The pull request that delivers the issue: its title and URL.
pull_request.name: pull_request

status.description: Current workflow state of the issue. A task's statuses (open, in_progress, in_review, done, cancelled) and two of its own: changes_requested (reviewed, with findings to fix; reads as in_progress on a task) and ready_to_merge (passed review, waiting to land; reads as in_review on a task). The flow is open, in_progress, in_review, back to changes_requested or on to ready_to_merge, then done, which means the change landed.
status.name: status

first_name.description: First name; optional — a person may exist before a name is set
first_name.name: first_name

last_name.description: Last name; optional — a person may exist before a name is set
last_name.name: last_name

reported_tasks->task/out.description: Tasks originally reported/created by this person
reported_tasks->task/out.name: reported_tasks

approach.description: Major components, dependencies and sequencing, tied to the spec's success criteria by name.
approach.name: approach

plan_status.description: draft while being written; approved once the requester has confirmed it, which requires its spec to be approved and is what lets its tasks start; superseded once a newer plan replaces it, which locks its fields.
plan_status.name: plan_status

risks.description: What could go wrong with this particular approach.
risks.name: risks

spec->spec/out.description: The spec this plan implements. One per plan; a spec accumulates plans as they are revised and superseded.
spec->spec/out.name: spec

tasks->task/out.description: Tasks that carry out this plan. A task belongs to one plan.
tasks->task/out.name: tasks

description.description: What this play automates, in one line
description.name: description

enabled.description: The user's on/off switch. The engine never changes it
enabled.name: enabled

rules.description: Rule definitions: each a trigger, conditions and actions
rules.name: rules

suspended_at.description: When the engine suspended the play on this device
suspended_at.name: suspended_at

suspended_message.description: The diagnostic the suspension was logged with
suspended_message.name: suspended_message

suspended_reason.description: Why the engine took the play out of service on this device
suspended_reason.name: suspended_reason

end_date.description: Date the project is intended to finish (or did finish). Paired with start_date to compute the project's planned or actual timeline; a project past its end_date while status is still active or planning reads as behind schedule.
end_date.name: end_date

priority.description: Relative importance for triage across projects (highest, high, medium, low, lowest) — the same scale as task priority. Sorting follows that order rather than the alphabetical order of the values; user-defined values sort after all of them. Absent means no priority has been assigned.
priority.name: priority

start_date.description: Date work on the project is intended to begin (or began). Used with end_date to compute the project's planned or actual timeline.
start_date.name: start_date

status.description: Current stage of the project: planning (not yet started), active (underway), completed (finished successfully), or cancelled (abandoned). Distinct from an individual task's status.
status.name: status

execution_count.description: Number of times query has been executed
execution_count.name: execution_count

generator_context.description: Parent chat ID for AI-generated queries
generator_context.name: generator_context

target_type.description: Target node type to query (* for all)
target_type.name: target_type

view_config.description: How the query renders: lastView (list, table or kanban) and kanban.groupBy
view_config.name: view_config

max_iterations.description: Maximum ReAct loop iterations for this skill
max_iterations.name: max_iterations

not_for.description: Requests that sound similar but belong to another skill.
not_for.name: not_for

role.description: tool: a capability the agent finds for a request. procedure: a way of working a record through its stages, handed over with the records it governs; skill search ranks it in its own lane and never lets it lead a request ahead of a tool skill.
role.name: role

tool_whitelist.description: Tools available when this skill is active
tool_whitelist.name: tool_whitelist

use_for.description: The requests this skill should handle, worded the way someone would ask. Short and specific.
use_for.name: use_for

applies_to->schema/out.description: Schemas this skill is about; a matched skill carries their definitions
applies_to->schema/out.name: applies_to

attached_to->/out.description: Nodes this skill is handed over with; reading one returns the skill
attached_to->/out.name: attached_to

checkout_path.description: The folder on this machine that holds the project's checkout. An agent session launched for the project runs there. It is set on each machine and stays on it.
checkout_path.name: checkout_path

repository.description: The project's source repository: its title and URL. A checkout of that repository belongs to this project.
repository.name: repository

boundaries.description: What may always be done without asking, what needs sign-off first, and what must never be done.
boundaries.name: boundaries

objective.description: What is being built, why, and for whom, in the requester's own terms, not a restatement of the title.
objective.name: objective

spec_status.description: draft while being written; approved once the requester has confirmed it, which needs at least one checkbox child as a success criterion and is what lets a plan against it be approved; superseded once a newer spec replaces it, which locks its fields.
spec_status.name: spec_status

decisions->decision/out.description: Decisions that govern the work under this spec
decisions->decision/out.name: decisions

tasks->task/out.description: Tasks this spec governs, linked directly so a task's spec is one hop away. A task may serve more than one spec.
tasks->task/out.name: tasks

completed_at.description: Date the task was finished. Set when status moves to done; used for completion-rate and cycle-time reporting alongside started_at. Absent while the task is open, in progress, or cancelled without a recorded finish date.
completed_at.name: completed_at

due_date.description: Date by which the task should be completed. Used for deadline reminders and overdue detection (a task is overdue when due_date is in the past and status is not done or cancelled). Absent means no deadline.
due_date.name: due_date

priority.description: Relative urgency for triage and sorting (highest, high, medium, low, lowest), independent of status. Sorting follows that urgency order rather than the alphabetical order of the values; user-defined values sort after all of them. Not a deadline — use due_date for that. Absent means no priority has been assigned.
priority.name: priority

started_at.description: Date work on the task actually began, distinct from due_date (the deadline) and created_at (when the task record was made). Set once, when status first moves to in_progress or in_review; not required.
started_at.name: started_at

status.description: Current workflow state of the task: open (not started), in_progress (actively being worked), in_review (the work is finished and waiting on review, typically an open pull request), done (completed), or cancelled (abandoned, not completed). Drives board columns and completion rollups — a task counts toward "done" totals only when this equals done.
status.name: status

blocks->task/out.description: Tasks that cannot start/complete until this task is done
blocks->task/out.name: blocks

decisions->decision/out.description: Decisions that govern how this task is done
decisions->decision/out.name: decisions

relates_to->task/out.description: Tasks this task is related to, with no directional dependency
relates_to->task/out.name: relates_to

description.description: What the tool does; embedded with its name for discovery
description.name: description

enabled.description: Whether the tool may be offered to the model; a native tool always is
enabled.name: enabled

parameter_schema.description: JSON Schema for the parameters the tool takes
parameter_schema.name: parameter_schema

cli_command.description: The `nodespace` command and subcommand that does what the tool does; unset when there is none
cli_command.name: cli_command

handler.description: Stable key resolving to the handler that runs the tool
handler.name: handler
